questions.question: Dr Ramdan's landlord is suing him for non-payment of rent. According to Article 26, what is the deadline to regularize the situation before eviction?
options: 3 days
15 days
30 days
3 months
questions.explanation: Art. 26, para. 2: the period is set at 15 days when the request is based on non-payment of rent.

questions.question: Dr Kamali received a notice for personal recovery but disputes the reason. According to case law, who bears the burden of proof?
options: The landlord must prove his good faith
The tenant must prove the landlord's bad faith
The court must verify good faith ex officio
The burden of proof lies with the court
questions.explanation: Case law requires the landlord to prove his good faith and the reality of his intention to repossess the premises.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan wishes to challenge the amount of the eviction compensation proposed by the landlord. According to Article 7, what recourse is available?
options: Seize the court of first instance
Seize the commercial court
Appeal to a court-appointed expert
Both first two recourses are possible
questions.explanation: The tenant may seize the court to challenge the compensation and request an expert appraisal if necessary.

questions.question: Dr Kamali's landlord refuses to pay the eviction compensation. According to Article 28, what can the tenant do?
options: Seize the court to obtain enforcement of the judgment
Remain in the premises until payment
Request a seizure of the landlord's assets
All of the above answers are correct
questions.explanation: Art. 28: the tenant may seize the court for enforcement of the judgment and benefit from enforcement procedures.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan carried out improvement works costing 300,000 DH. According to Article 7, are these works included in the eviction compensation?
options: Yes, provided proof is provided
No, works are not compensated
Yes, only if amortized over 5 years
No, only the value of the business is taken into account
questions.explanation: Art. 7, para. 3: the compensation includes works expenses, subject to their justification.

questions.question: Dr Kamali assigned his lease without complying with the notification formalities. According to Article 25, what does he risk?
options: The assignment is unenforceable against the landlord
The landlord may terminate the lease
The assignee may be evicted
All of the above answers are correct
questions.explanation: Art. 25, para. 3: the assignment is only enforceable against the lessor from the date of notification. In the absence, the assignment is unenforceable.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan's landlord included a resolutory clause in the lease. According to Article 33, how is this clause implemented?
options: It applies automatically in case of arrears
It requires a prior formal notice of 15 days
It is null and void by law
It must be approved by the court
questions.explanation: Art. 33: the resolutory clause requires a formal notice remaining unsuccessful for 15 days.

questions.question: Dr Kamali wishes to use the summary procedure to challenge an abusive notice. According to Law 49-16, is this possible?
options: Yes, the summary judge may rule urgently
No, notice disputes must be heard on the merits
Yes, but only in matters of neighbor disputes
No, summary procedure does not exist in commercial lease matters
questions.explanation: The summary judge may be seized in case of urgency to suspend the effects of an abusive notice.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan was evicted without compensation even though he was entitled to renewal. According to case law, how can he be compensated?
options: By awarding damages for abusive procedure
By nullifying the notice
By payment of the eviction compensation with interest
All of the above answers are possible
questions.explanation: Case law offers several avenues of recourse: nullity of the notice, eviction compensation, damages.

questions.question: Dr Kamali faced a bad faith landlord who simulated a personal recovery. According to Article 26, what sanctions are possible?
options: Nullity of the notice
Payment of eviction compensation
Damages for abusive procedure
All of the above sanctions are possible
questions.explanation: The landlord's bad faith exposes him to nullity of the notice, payment of compensation, and damages.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan wishes to appeal a decision of the court of first instance. According to civil procedure, what is the appeal period?
options: 15 days
1 month
2 months
3 months
questions.explanation: The appeal period in commercial lease matters is generally 15 days.

questions.question: Dr Kamali's landlord obtained an eviction judgment but does not pay the compensation. According to Article 28, what can the tenant do?
options: Request forced execution of the judgment
Remain in the premises until payment
Request seizure of rents due by the landlord
All of these actions are possible
questions.explanation: Art. 28: the tenant may request forced execution, remain in the premises, or seize rents.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan received a notice for demolition-reconstruction but the building permit has not yet been issued. According to Article 18, what must the landlord do?
options: Wait for the permit before serving the notice
Serve the notice and produce the permit later
Serve the notice without a permit, as the permit is optional
Request a derogation from the court
questions.explanation: Art. 18: the landlord must produce a valid building permit. The notice is null if the permit is not issued.

questions.question: Dr Kamali challenges the valuation of his business. According to Article 7, which method of proof is most admissible?
options: Accounting expertise
Real estate agent valuation
Tax declaration of the last 4 financial years
Landlord's estimate
questions.explanation: Art. 7, para. 3: the compensation is calculated on the basis of the tax declarations of the last four financial years, which are authoritative.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan's landlord assigned the building during an eviction procedure. According to Article 26 bis, what are the consequences on the procedure?
options: The procedure automatically lapses
The procedure continues against the new owner
The procedure must be restarted from scratch
The tenant must summon the new owner
questions.explanation: Art. 26 bis: the new owner is required to respect existing leases. The procedure continues against him.

questions.question: Dr Kamali was illegally evicted by the landlord. According to case law, can the tenant request specific compensation?
options: Yes, for disturbance of enjoyment
Yes, for commercial loss
Yes, for relocation costs
Yes, all of these compensations are possible
questions.explanation: In case of illegal eviction, the tenant may obtain several compensations: disturbance of enjoyment, commercial loss, relocation costs.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan wishes to have a clause in his lease declared null by the court. According to the code of civil procedure, what action must he bring?
options: An action for nullity
A summary procedure
A declaratory action
An ordinary court action
questions.explanation: The action for nullity is the appropriate action to have a clause declared null.

questions.question: Dr Kamali's landlord brought an action for validation of the notice. According to Article 27, can the tenant request compensation before the judgment?
options: Yes, during the validation action
No, he must wait for the final judgment
Yes, only after eviction
No, compensation must be requested on appeal
questions.explanation: Art. 27, para. 2: the tenant may file a request for compensation during the action for validation of the notice.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan and the landlord reached an amicable agreement. According to Law 49-16, is this agreement valid?
options: Yes, subject to public policy provisions
No, only the court can validate an agreement
Yes, only with the agreement of a lawyer
No, settlement is prohibited in lease matters
questions.explanation: Amicable agreements are valid provided they respect the public policy provisions of Law 49-16.

questions.question: Dr Kamali won his appeal. According to civil procedure, is an appeal to the Court of Cassation possible in commercial lease matters?
options: Yes, but only for questions of law
No, the appeal is the final instance
Yes, cassation is always possible
No, the appeal decision is final
questions.explanation: Appeal to the Court of Cassation is possible for questions of law, even in commercial lease matters.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan was summoned to appear. According to civil procedure, what is the appearance period in commercial lease matters?
options: 8 days
15 days
1 month
2 months
questions.explanation: The appearance period is generally 15 days in commercial lease matters.

questions.question: Dr Kamali's landlord served a payment order. According to Article 33, what is a payment order?
options: A simple informal request
A bailiff's act putting the tenant on notice to pay
A judicial procedure
A simple registered letter
questions.explanation: Art. 33: the payment order is a bailiff's act putting the tenant on notice to pay.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan wishes to challenge a payment order. According to civil procedure, what recourse is possible?
options: Seize the court to challenge the validity of the order
Ignore the order
Pay to avoid a conflict
Request a stay of payment
questions.explanation: The tenant may seize the court to challenge the validity of the payment order.

questions.question: Dr Kamali obtained a court-appointed expert appraisal. According to the code of civil procedure, what is the purpose of the expert appraisal?
options: To enlighten the court on technical questions
To speed up the procedure
To allow an amicable agreement
All of these answers are correct
questions.explanation: The expert appraisal enlightens the court on technical questions and may facilitate an amicable agreement.

questions.question: Dr Ramdan finally obtained satisfaction in court. According to Article 28, what compensation can he expect?
options: The full amount of eviction compensation
Damages for the loss suffered
Reimbursement of his legal costs
All of these compensations are possible
questions.explanation: Art. 28: the tenant may obtain eviction compensation, damages, and reimbursement of legal costs.
